results.name: shared_ones_digit_outside_gap
results.description: In sets of >=2 examples, among non-example targets 1-20 outside the span, yes-rate for targets sharing a ones digit with some example minus those sharing none; observed above null means people use digit-level similarity to examples beyond what the model's ends-in-d rules (which need all examples to share the digit) capture.
results.code:
# name: shared_ones_digit_outside_gap
# description: In sets of >=2 examples, among non-example targets 1-20 outside the span, yes-rate for targets sharing a ones digit with some example minus those sharing none; observed above null means people use digit-level similarity to examples beyond what the model's ends-in-d rules (which need all examples to share the digit) capture.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    od = np.mod(X, 10)
    share = (od == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    near = (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 20) & (n >= 2) & ~is_ex
    a = near & share
    b = near & ~share
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: min_first_below_contrast
results.description: Among sets of >=2 examples, yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the minimum when the minimum is shown first minus when it is shown later; observed less negative than null means the incumbent's first-shown-bottom credit exaggerates the opening-order effect, more negative means people show a stronger order effect than the model.
results.code:
# name: min_first_below_contrast
# description: Among sets of >=2 examples, yes-rate for targets 1-10 below the minimum when the minimum is shown first minus when it is shown later; observed less negative than null means the incumbent's first-shown-bottom credit exaggerates the opening-order effect, more negative means people show a stronger order effect than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    first_min = X[:, 0] == mn
    below = (mn - t >= 1) & (mn - t <= 10) & (n >= 2)
    a = below & first_min
    b = below & ~first_min
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: largest_gap_interior_yes
results.description: In sets of >=3 examples, yes-rate for non-example targets inside the span that fall in the largest gap between adjacent sorted examples minus those in the other gaps; observed below null means people treat widely separated example clusters as separate groups (not one range) more than the model, above null means the opposite.
results.code:
# name: largest_gap_interior_yes
# description: In sets of >=3 examples, yes-rate for non-example targets inside the span that fall in the largest gap between adjacent sorted examples minus those in the other gaps; observed below null means people treat widely separated example clusters as separate groups (not one range) more than the model, above null means the opposite.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    S = np.sort(X, axis=1)  # NaN sorted last
    lo = S[:, :-1]
    hi = S[:, 1:]
    gaps = np.where(np.isnan(hi) | np.isnan(lo), -1.0, hi - lo)
    gi = np.argmax(gaps, axis=1)
    rows = np.arange(len(t))
    glo = lo[rows, gi]
    ghi = hi[rows, gi]
    inside = (t > mn) & (t < mx) & ~is_ex & (n >= 3)
    in_big = (t > glo) & (t < ghi)
    a = inside & in_big
    b = inside & ~in_big
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: divisor_target_below_gap
results.description: For non-example targets 2 or more below the smallest example, yes-rate for targets that divide some example (factors, e.g. 5 or 19 after 95) minus non-divisor targets in the same below-span region; observed above null means people generalize to factors of the examples, a concept absent from the model's hypothesis space.
results.code:
# name: divisor_target_below_gap
# description: For non-example targets 2 or more below the smallest example, yes-rate for targets that divide some example (factors, e.g. 5 or 19 after 95) minus non-divisor targets in the same below-span region; observed above null means people generalize to factors of the examples, a concept absent from the model's hypothesis space.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    Xf = np.nan_to_num(X, nan=0.0).astype(np.int64)
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)
    tt = np.maximum(t, 1)[:, None]
    divs = (valid & (np.mod(Xf, tt) == 0)).any(axis=1) & (t >= 2)
    below = (mn - t >= 2) & ~is_ex & (t >= 2)
    a = below & divs
    b = below & ~divs
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: single_digit_target_far_yes
results.description: Yes-rate for single-digit non-example targets (1-9) when every example is >= 20; observed above null means people include small numbers more than the model, below null means people treat 'two-digit numbers' as a category boundary the model's ranges/rules over-cross.
results.code:
# name: single_digit_target_far_yes
# description: Yes-rate for single-digit non-example targets (1-9) when every example is >= 20; observed above null means people include small numbers more than the model, below null means people treat 'two-digit numbers' as a category boundary the model's ranges/rules over-cross.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)

results.name: prime_vs_odd_composite_gap
results.description: In sets of >=2 examples that are all primes, yes-rate for prime non-example targets minus odd composite targets (excluding 1); observed above null means people favour primality more sharply than the model's prime-vs-odd competition predicts, below null means people treat such sets as 'odd numbers' more than the model.
results.code:
# name: prime_vs_odd_composite_gap
# description: In sets of >=2 examples that are all primes, yes-rate for prime non-example targets minus odd composite targets (excluding 1); observed above null means people favour primality more sharply than the model's prime-vs-odd competition predicts, below null means people treat such sets as 'odd numbers' more than the model.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    N = np.arange(101)
    isp = np.ones(101, dtype=bool); isp[:2] = False
    for k in range(2, 11):
        isp[k * k::k] = False
    Xf = np.nan_to_num(X, nan=0.0).astype(np.int64)
    allp = (isp[Xf] | np.isnan(X)).all(axis=1) & (n >= 2)
    tp = isp[t]
    oddc = (np.mod(t, 2) == 1) & ~tp & (t > 1)
    a = allp & ~is_ex & tp
    b = allp & ~is_ex & oddc
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: progression_residue_gap
results.description: In sets of >=3 examples whose pairwise differences share a gcd g in 3-12 (g!=10) with nonzero residue (e.g. 41,47,53: 5 mod 6), yes-rate for non-example targets congruent to the examples mod g minus non-congruent targets of the same parity class; observed above null means people pick up 'same step/offset' progressions the model (which only has residue-0 multiples) misses.
results.code:
# name: progression_residue_gap
# description: In sets of >=3 examples whose pairwise differences share a gcd g in 3-12 (g!=10) with nonzero residue (e.g. 41,47,53: 5 mod 6), yes-rate for non-example targets congruent to the examples mod g minus non-congruent targets of the same parity class; observed above null means people pick up 'same step/offset' progressions the model (which only has residue-0 multiples) misses.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    Xf = np.nan_to_num(X, nan=0.0).astype(np.int64)
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)
    x0 = Xf[:, :1]
    diffs = np.where(valid, np.abs(Xf - x0), 0)
    g = np.gcd.reduce(diffs, axis=1)
    x0 = x0[:, 0]
    ok = (n >= 3) & (g >= 3) & (g <= 12) & (g != 10)
    gs = np.where(ok, g, 1)
    res = np.mod(x0, gs)
    ok &= res != 0
    cong = np.mod(t, gs) == res
    same_par = np.where(np.mod(gs, 2) == 0, np.mod(t, 2) == np.mod(x0, 2), True)
    a = ok & ~is_ex & cong
    b = ok & ~is_ex & ~cong & same_par
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: scale_extreme_target_yes
results.description: Yes-rate for non-example targets at the ends of the scale (1-5 or 96-100) lying at least 15 beyond the example span; observed above null means people treat scale endpoints (e.g. 100, 1) as special inclusions the model's interval/rule hypotheses do not produce, below null means the model over-extends ranges to the scale ends.
results.code:
# name: scale_extreme_target_yes
# description: Yes-rate for non-example targets at the ends of the scale (1-5 or 96-100) lying at least 15 beyond the example span; observed above null means people treat scale endpoints (e.g. 100, 1) as special inclusions the model's interval/rule hypotheses do not produce, below null means the model over-extends ranges to the scale ends.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(" ", "", regex=False).str.split(",", expand=True)
    X = X.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values.astype(float)
    n = (~np.isnan(X)).sum(axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    is_ex = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    dist = np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx)
    m = ((t <= 5) | (t >= 96)) & (dist >= 15) & ~is_ex
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0
